how I think

Understand first. Build second.

I like technical work most when it starts with a real business problem and ends with something people can trust. My process is less “jump into the tool” and more “understand the system, the data, and the people around it.”

my working loop

From vague problem to reliable system.

01

Acknowledge the problem

Recognize the issue quickly, separate symptoms from the real business question, and decide what deserves attention first.

  • What changed?
  • Who is affected?
  • What would a useful outcome look like?
02

Collect the right information

Gather the key data points, understand the systems behind them, and map the process before deciding on a solution.

  • Source systems
  • Business rules
  • Ownership & handovers
03

Analyse deeply

Combine business context with technical analysis. Look for patterns, edge cases, missing definitions, and the points where trust breaks down.

  • Data quality
  • Process gaps
  • Root-cause analysis
04

Propose the solution

Explain the approach in plain language: what will change, why it should work, what the trade-offs are, and what needs approval before implementation.

  • Architecture
  • Impact
  • Agreement before build
05

Implement carefully

Optimise the query, model, report, integration, or workflow while keeping the solution understandable and maintainable.

  • Build
  • Test
  • Document
06

Complete, verify, support

Check that the result actually solves the original problem, make necessary adjustments, and leave the system easier to operate than before.

  • Validation
  • Handover
  • Continuous improvement

what I value

The principles I keep coming back to.

01

Start from scratch and finish

I enjoy taking an unclear problem all the way to something usable.

02

Improve repeating tasks

Repetition is usually a signal that a process can be made lighter.

03

Connect related data

Useful insight often appears when separate systems are understood together.

04

Communicate effectively

A solution is stronger when the people using it understand the logic behind it.

05

Share data literacy

Good data work should make other people more capable, not more dependent.

06

Design with responsibility

Business systems affect people, so technical decisions deserve context and care.
